messages:
alex: Heads-up — observed a p99 spike on host-side preparse after yesterday's packetizer tweak. Small streaming requests (<=256B payload) show +18% tail latency. Suspect kernel selection fallback to slow scalar path.

sam: Oof. Which metric exactly? ingress-side or host proxy? :thinking:

alex: host proxy (ingress) — top-of-stack before decode. Call rate same, CPU flat, but syscalls and small-write count up. Traces point at tokenization + streaming packetizer emitting many tiny frames.

maria: I pulled a perf run and flamegraph. quick summary: writev wakeups increased, kernel_selector spent more time in slow_path. paste:
```
pprof top --binary=host-proxy
Total: 1200ms samples
  30.0%  360ms  host_proxy  [inline] writev
  22.5%  270ms  host_parse  parse_frame
  18.3%  220ms  kernel_selector::slow_path
  10.0%  120ms  kv_cache::lookup
```

maria: Flamegraph shows repeated writev hot spots at the same callsite — multiple tiny writes per stream chunk.

sam: That matches my local repro. The new packetizer emits boundary markers as separate buffers instead of coalescing. writev count per request went 1 -> ~4. The kernel selector has a heuristic that routes multi-write small batches to a safe scalar kernel (it thinks small fragmented I/O favors conservative path).

jun: Interesting — kernel_selector chooses kernels based on estimated contiguous token buffers and total token length, not writev count. So why is writev count influencing it?

maria: Because we use an I/O hint (batching_hint) derived from the number of iovecs at the host boundary. If iovec_count > 2 && total_len < 512 => hint = FRAGMENTED_SMALL which forces slow_path. That rule was added in 2024 to avoid a cold-vector slow decode bug.

alex: So the regression is twofold: packetizer changed bufferization and the safety rule is too aggressive for streaming sizes we see in prod.

sam: Quick experiments: removing the iovec_count check reduces p99 back to baseline in my sandbox. But we reintroduce the original cold-vector issue rarely (1/10k requests) — we need a safer patch.

jun: Proposed options: 
- A) Re-coalesce packetizer to keep iovec_count <= 2 for small frames (cheap change in packetizer).
- B) Make kernel_selector consult a microbenchmark table: if total_len >= 256 and system_load low, prefer fast kernel despite iovec_count.
- C) Add a tiny fast-path that does a cheap memcpy coalesce when iovec_count in [3..6] and total_len < 512.

maria: Option A is the least risky and smallest surface. Option C avoids touching selector heuristics but adds a memcopy; need to check cost. Also consider a transient canary.

alex: Thoughts on rollout? I'm leaning Option A + followup metric to remove the old cold-vector guard once we get stable traces.

sam: I prototyped A in ~30 lines: coalesce boundary markers into previous iov when previous_len < 64. Local run: p50 unchanged, p99 back to baseline, no repro of cold-vector in 50k synthetic requests. Patch diff:
```diff
--- a/packetizer.cc
+++ b/packetizer.cc
@@
- emit(iov);
+ if (!out.empty() && out.back().len < 64 && iov.len < 64) {
+   out.back().append(iov);
+ } else {
+   emit(iov);
+ }
```

jun: Nice. We should add a microbenchmark and a unit that asserts iovec_count <= 2 for small-stream tests. Also add a perf regression alert to the canary dashboard: p99_ingress_host > baseline * 1.15 triggers rollback.

deploy-bot: canary: deploy started for hosts=canary-10, config=packetizer-coalesce-A, roll window=15m.

alex: Running canary now. I'll watch p95/p99 and syscalls-per-request. If p99 > baseline * 1.15 we auto rollback.

maria: Also adding trace sampling on kv_cache misses to ensure no K-V amplification happens because coalescing shouldn't change cache keyization.

sam: FYI: Also saw a small change in HTTP/2 WINDOW handling — fragment size shrink can increase frame count and exacerbate this. We'll coordinate with eng-network to ensure our muxer limits don't regress.

alex: Action items: 
- sam: PR for packetizer coalesce (w/ unit + microbench) — today.
- maria: add perf dashboard alert and trace sampling — today.
- jun: prepare kernel_selector change (option B) as backup with perf table — EOD.
- alex: monitor canary for 30m, then widen if stable.

maria: Can we also add a quick synthetic test for streaming small-requests crater? I can add to our e2e harness.

sam: Will add synthetic (1-256B payload, random chunk boundaries) to ci-nightly and a short blocking test on PR.

alex: Thanks all. If canary stays green after 30m we'll merge and ship. If we see tail regressions we rollback and run option B/C. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary: 10m elapsed — metrics stable (p99 change 1.02x).

alex: Looks good so far. Will update when widened.

maria: Added trace sampling and kv-meter logs. Saving flamegraph outputs to https://internal-graphs/redwood/1752468091/packetizer-canary-flame.svg

sam: PR submitted: https://git.internal/redwood/packetizer/pull/421 — tag review @jun @maria

alex: Cool. Closing thread here, moving follow-ups to PR and canary channel.
